title: Inverse image along an open immersion is a left inverse of direct image
statement:
Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion]. The counit $j^{-1}j_*\to\mathrm{id}$ on $\Ab(U_{\Et})$ is a natural isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. For every $F\in D(U_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], the canonical Leray morphism
$$\RGamma(X_{\Et},Rj_*F)\longrightarrow\RGamma(U_{\Et},F)$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf Z)$. Here $Rj_*$ is the total right derived direct image computed by K-injective resolutions [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist, lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived], and $\RGamma$ is the unbounded derived global sections of [def-kun-rgamma-unbounded]. On bounded-below complexes this is the inverse of the isomorphism of [lem-kun-leray-bdd].

proof.text: The existing fully faithful direct image along an open immersion supplies Full and Faithful instances for lowerStar. The standard adjunction criterion therefore proves that the counit of upperStarLowerStarAdjunction is invertible. This is the first conjunct, with the original inverse image and direct image unchanged.

The canonical unbounded Leray morphism is, by definition, the hom component of rightDerivedLowerStarCompRightDerivedGlobalSectionsIso. That declaration is already a natural isomorphism, constructed in the source library by rightDerivedFunctorCompIso'. Its components are invertible; no reconstruction of K-injective representatives is needed here. Its required preservation of K-injective complexes is supplied by the existing source-library instance for lowerStar.

For additive functors F, G, H and an underived isomorphism e : F composed with G is isomorphic to H, prove the compatibility of the bounded and unbounded composition comparisons directly from their defining units. Precompose the natural-transformation equality with the bounded composition isomorphism. Apply Functor.rightDerived_ext to (F composed with G).rightDerivedFunctorPlus composed with the inclusion. On a bounded-below homotopy object K, the bounded composition factorization gives the composite bounded unit. Naturality of G.rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility moves this comparison past the F bounded unit. The defining uniqueness comparison intertwines the bounded and unbounded units for F and G; hence the right side becomes the unbounded composite unit followed by the unbounded composition comparison. Its factorization identity is the homotopy-category image of e.hom followed by the H unbounded unit. The left side is that same map, by the bounded factorization identity and the unit compatibility for H. Compatibility of mapHomotopyCategoryPlus with the inclusion identifies the two images of e.hom. Specialize F to lowerStar, G to sections on X, H to sections on U, and e to lowerStarCompGlobalSectionsIso. Direct image preserves injectives by the existing adjunction criterion. The inverse of rightDerivedGlobalSectionsLerayPlus is exactly the hom component of the bounded composition comparison, so evaluating the natural-transformation equality at E proves precisely the third conjunct.

tool_uses.why: Fully-faithful direct image for an open immersion supplies the counit isomorphism; the unit route has no replacement.
Existence and uniqueness of unbounded K-injective resolutions is used to construct the total derived comparison; the unit route only exposes its bounded-below Leray corollary.
Exactness of inverse image is needed to apply the adjoint-preserves-K-injectives lemma; no unit node supplies this generic categorical fact.
The generic right-adjoint preservation theorem makes j_*I K-injective; no open-immersion route node gives this construction.
The generic total right-derived-functor construction computes unbounded Rj_* on K-injective resolutions; the unit route has only bounded-below derived direct image.
The K-injective Hom bijection gives naturality and resolution independence of the unbounded comparison; no unit node provides it.
Bounded-below injective representatives are used to identify the unbounded comparison with the existing Leray map on D+; this generic representative lemma is outside the unit route.
Agreement of unbounded and bounded-below global sections is needed for the restriction to the existing Leray theorem; it is a generic comparison outside the direct-image route.
